chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: The Charleston, Plantation Club and Jungle Casino
summary: Albertson recalls the origin of the Charleston dance and the Jungle Casino; Hunter thinks Florence Mills was at the Plantation and says she went to Europe in 1925.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Do you remember the -- I think it

the club was called the Charleston. Now, there was this group called the Charlestonians. There was a club downtown or midtown -- James P. Johnson. Remember when he wrote the Charleston, and it became the big dance fad?
Well, wasn't that the Plantation Club where Florence Mills was?
Was that the Plantation Club?
I think so. I think it was the Plantation where Florence worked.
Uh-huh.
Uh-huh.
Looking in this book --
Uh-huh, I'm almost positive it was the Plantation.
The Jungle Casino.
I don't remember.
You don't remember the Jungle Casino?
It was on West 64th Street --
See, most --
-- and a lot of black people from Charleston, South Carolina, used to come up there, used to frequent that place. And they would do variations on cotillion steps --
Oh, uh-huh.
-- which was the start of the --
Charleston.
-- the Charleston.
Well, I must have been in Europe then, you know, but what -- when was that?
That would have been -- well, that would have been around 1925, I think.
Uh-huh. See, I left, went to Europe in '25, I think, my first trip.
